title: A Fixed Particle Test for Computation in a Forced Viscous Flow
main_claim: Theorem 1: from a machine M and a word w, an algorithm builds a smooth, mean-zero (optionally solenoidal) force on T^3 at a fixed computable viscosity, starting from zero velocity. Every mixed derivative of the velocity and of the force is in L^inf ∩ L^2 in time (sup norm in space). The NS solution is unique among classical solutions. The particle starting at (1/8,3/8,0) enters {1/2<x<1} if and only if M halts on w.
coverage:
Checked all of main.tex, analytic-tools.tex and analytic-appendix.tex.
- Tape code: odd digits in base B=2m+1, intervals I_a with gaps of 1/B, unique decoding.
- State boxes: c(q_i)+kappa < 1/4 for nonhalting states; the halting box is [3/4,13/16] and sits inside O; K = [1/8,13/16]x[3/8,7/16].
- Branch table for R/L/S moves: the linear part is diag(lambda, 1/lambda) with lambda = 1/B, B, 1.
- Path Psi: the x-coordinate is a convex combination of the endpoints, and the reciprocal-convexity bound on y keeps the moving rectangle inside the convex hull of source and target. So nonhalting-to-nonhalting paths stay in x<=1/4.
- Hamiltonian: verified symbolically that V_j = (E_x+gamma(x-C_x), E_y-gamma(y-C_y)) equals dPsi/ds. Checked that chi = eta_K^{1/32} is supported inside the unit square.
- Recorder: the enlarged supports of the R_j cutoffs (enlargement kappa/(4B)) are disjoint; the half-period shift gives G mean zero and misses every R_j; G=j on R_j.
- Gates: b_j supports are disjoint mod 1, and Lambda^n z_n is an integer, so only the newest digit is read.
- Timing: theta collars make the loader, recorder and planar stages disjoint and smooth at the joins; t_n >= 1+2n.
- Derivative bound C S_n^{-1-h} Lambda^{n mu_z} with S_n=2^{n^2} gives the L^2 sums; the force products use one L^inf factor and one L^2 factor; f has mean zero.
- Uniqueness via Gronwall on the energy difference; noncompact cutoff errors.
- Fourier projection: |k|^{-5} decay times O(n^2) shell size gives a summable n^{-3} tail.
- Effective-evaluation lemma and the inequality Lambda^{2n mu} <= 2^{n^2/2}.
- Loader stays in K, and the case of an initially halted input.
sibling_notes: Self-contained: it explicitly does not rely on the Stationary companion. It uses the same ingredients as siblings in family 376 (history in the z-coordinate, curl/Hamiltonian realization, Leray-type uniqueness). Sibling reviews were all no_gap_found.
